newsitem.title: FRANCE: Six groups bid for French all-cargo transport hub.
newsitem.headline: Six groups bid for French all-cargo transport hub.

text.p: The semi-public company managing the Europort Vatry all-cargo transport centre project said six private sector candidates had been short-listed to run the multi-modal site.

The Conseil General de la Marne public authority is investing one billion francs over the next two years in transforming the ex-NATO airfield into a new platform for full-freighter activities by air,road and rail.
The site is situated around 150 kilometres east of Paris at Vatry.
The six candidates, grouped into French, international and Franco-international consortia, were presented at a press conference in Paris earlier Tuesday.

The three French bids are: Via Generale de Transport de l'Industrie (VIA-GTI), freight handling installations operator Sogaris and the Toulouse airport authority; secondly Penauille Polyservices (part of Generale des Prestations) and thirdly Compagnie Generale des Eaux, French regional carrier Air Littoral and the Nice Cote d'Azur airport authority.
The only solely international bid is from Amsterdam airport's, Schiphol Management Services (SMS).

Franco-international candidates are: Montreal airport, Pingat/SNC Lavalin, the Chambers of Commerce in Rheims, Epernay, Chalons sur Marne and Troyes as well as airline services company Ienair; and lastly the U.S. based Airport Group International together with French companies SAUR (part of the Bougyues group, Cegelec, Geodis, as well as Sodearif, Sofreavia(Ste Francaise d'Etudes et de Realisations d'Equipements Aeronautiques), Sopardel and French oil group Total.
The six candidates must submit their bids by September 1 1997 with the winning bid announced during the final quarter of 1997, although a shortlist of two is also possible.
A joint bid by two of the candidate groups is not being ruled at this stage, an industry source said Tuesday.

"The opening of the airport is fixed for mid-1998 with the first all-cargo flights scheduled to operate from this date or at the latest by the end 1998, Europort Vatry told Reuters earlier this year."
The project is targeting the major air cargo markets such as North America, the Far East, the Gulf States and Europe.

According to market surveys commissioned by Europort Vatry, the all-cargo airport could generate between 300,000 and 700,000 tonnes of air cargo annually by 2010 in capturing part of the growing volume of freight traffic destined to be handled at Europe's seven leading airports over the next 15 years.
